h1: Role of Government and NGOs in Reclaiming Play Spaces Across India

props.title: Role of Government and NGOs in Reclaiming Play Spaces Across India
props.summaryText: Governments plan and fund, NGOs mobilise communities, companies fund through CSR. How each can help reclaim and create play spaces, and why maintenance must be part of every plan.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Children playing on spring riders at a public play area

takeaways.text: Municipal bodies control the most land and can plan play into parks, streets and redevelopment.
NGOs and community groups bring local knowledge, mobilise residents and help keep spaces cared for.
Company CSR programmes can fund playgrounds in schools and under-served areas.
Every project needs a maintenance plan and owner, or the space is lost again.

faq.q: How can government help create play spaces?
faq.a: By protecting open land in city plans, including play in parks, streets and redevelopment projects, funding equipment and maintenance, and writing clear tenders for durable, safe equipment.

faq.q: How can NGOs help reclaim play spaces?
faq.a: By working with communities to identify spaces, involving children in design, organising events such as play streets, and helping residents look after the space.

faq.q: Can companies fund playgrounds through CSR?
faq.a: Companies in India can support projects for education, child welfare and community development through CSR, and many fund playgrounds in schools and under-served communities. Check the eligible activities with your CSR team.
